# Simpsons paradox

## Pre-lab lecture
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw(16))
```

Choose the parameters
```{r}
beta_0 <- 10 # Y intercept
beta_1 <- 0.1 # Additional typo per increase in typing speed
beta_2 <- -10 # Difference between typist B and the reference level A
sigma <- 3 # SD of the residuals
```

Generate predictors
- For simpson's paradox there must be a correlation between the predictors
```{r}
# Sample size
N <- 30

# Typist identities
typist <- sample(c("A", "B"), N, replace = TRUE) # 30 values of A and B

# Dummy variable for typist B
typistB <- ifelse(typist == "B", 1, 0)

# KEY PART: Create relationship between predictors
# Continuous predictor variable dependent on categorical variable
typing_speed <- rnorm(N, mean = ifelse(typist == "B", 100, 45), sd = 15) # Tying speed random, but expected mean changes with categorical
```

Calculate the expected value of the response
```{r}
expected_typos <- beta_0 + beta_1 * typing_speed + beta_2 * typistB
```

Simulate the response variable
```{r}
typos <- rnorm(
  n = N,
  mean = expected_typos,
  sd = sigma
)
```

Visualize
```{r}
simulated_typing <- tibble(typing_speed, typos, typist)

ggplot(simulated_typing, aes(typing_speed, typos, fill = typist)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, shape = 21)
```

Fit and interpret
```{r}
# Only look at typing speed
one_predictor_lm <- lm(typos ~ typing_speed, simulated_typing)
summary(one_predictor_lm)

# Negative relationship
```


```{r}
# Look at both typing speed and the typist
two_predictor_lm <- lm(typos ~ typing_speed + typist, simulated_typing)
summary(two_predictor_lm)

# Positive relationship
```
